text:
jordan: :rotating_light: seeing a spike in 5xx and tail latency from prompt-router v2 canary, started at ~3923456789
incident-bot: Alert: prompt-router-v2-canary errors > 5% for 3m. Pager dispatched to @oncall. See /incidents/3923456789
lee: grabbing logs, looks like kernel selection mismatch causing OOMs on a subset of hosts
tara: confirmed, 3 hosts in canary pool are evicting due to mmap failures, client retries piling up
jordan: rolling the feature gate down for canary group now. Command: ffctl toggle route_v2_canary --env prod --set false
oncall-bot: Executing toggle: route_v2_canary -> false (initiated by jordan)
mike: copying a quick customer-facing note: "We detected an elevated error rate for prompt routing on a new canary. We paused the rollout and are investigating. No data exposure."
lee: quick mitigation plan: 1) route fallback to stable v1 2) drain affected hosts 3) rollback kernel patch if found
tara: @jordan after toggle we're still seeing increased latency for some sessions that were routed earlier. Can you trigger immediate route-level circuit on the edge?
jordan: edge circuit engaged: curl -X POST https://ops.internal/edge/circuit -d '{"route":"prompt","action":"cut"}'
oncall-bot: edge circuit accepted, routing fallback to prompt-v1 applied :white_check_mark:
mike: paging SRE for host drain, @lee can you run the drain script?
lee: running: ./scripts/drain-hosts --hosts host-22,host-27,host-31 --reason "canary mmap failures"
incident-bot: Note: we're also increasing observability retention for this thread for 2h per SRE request
jordan: running canary diagnostics: kernel logs show "failed to allocate anon_vma" on host-27; attaching snippet:
```
[  123.456789] prompt_runtime[4312]: mmap failed: -12
[  123.456791] prompt_runtime[4312]: kv_cache_alloc failed
```
lee: that aligns with a recent glibc tweak in the runtime image shipped with v2. Workaround: pin old runtime or use a different allocator
tara: decision: abort rollout, pin runtime on canary to previous image, re-enable canary when validated. Also open customer incident doc and notify CS for top 10 customers in affected regions
mike: noted. I'll post to status.redwood.ai: "We paused an experimental prompt routing rollout after elevated errors. Stable routing is restored. Investigating root cause."
jordan: action items logged in the incident doc. Handing off to SRE for postmortem, paging @lee and @mike for follow-ups. Back to normal ops once hosts drain and canary traffic is 0
lee: host drains in progress, will confirm when KG metrics show zero canary traffic
oncall-bot: Handoff: oncall clear, transitioning to follow-up cadence. If anything regresses, repage the oncall channel.
mike: customer comms sent for customers with >1000 daily active prompts, CS ack'd. Marking as mitigated for now :white_check_mark:
jordan: thanks team. Postmortem ticket created: PM-3121. We'll plan a rollback of the runtime change and a tighter kernel/allocator test before any rerun of the canary.
